content.text: No non-compete, field-of-use, territory, or exclusivity restriction binding our side exists anywhere in the agreement; the only hits are "court of competent jurisdiction" and generic no-conflict representations.

input.quote: Section 3.1 Engagement. The Issuer engages Cellco as the Servicer of the Receivables for the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee, and Cellco accepts this engagement.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no non-compete, field-of-use, territory or exclusivity covenant binding the Issuer or the Depositor, so the preferred position is met. Searches for "compete", "competing", "exclusive", "field of use", "engage", "solicit", "restriction" and "prohibited" across Articles I–XI and the schedules return only (i) "court of competent jurisdiction" references (p0335, p0469), (ii) generic no-conflict representations that performance will not contravene "any contractual restriction binding on or affecting it or its property" (p0240, p0266, p0279), and (iii) the Cap Collateral Account "exclusive control" account-control mechanic (p0387–p0388), none of which limit the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The Servicer engagement in Section 3.1 is not stated to be exclusive, and the successor-servicer provisions expressly contemplate our engaging another institution to service the Receivables (p0334, p0346). The restrictions we do carry — Section 9.2 (no transfer or Lien on Depositor Transferred Property), Section 9.5 (no petition) and Section 9.6 (limited recourse) — are structural securitization covenants protecting the transaction's bankruptcy-remote status, not restrictive covenants against competing activity, and Section 7.3's limit on the Servicer's obligation to license its own software is a restriction on Cellco's obligations rather than on our business. No redline is proposed.
